source.publication: 2025 Schedule M1M Income Additions and Subtractions
source.section: Form M1 lines 1-4, 7-10 (instructions PDF p.13 Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.14 Worksheet A, p.39 Tax Rate Schedules, pp.32-38 tax table); Schedule M1M line 12 and Worksheet for line 12 steps 1-30 (M1M PDF p.3, p.4)

worked: Joint AGI under 108,320: all of line 6b; age subtraction long gone. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution 66,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 = 100,000.00. Social Security benefits (Form 1040 line 6a) 40,000.00; line 6b taxable 34,000.00 (federal worksheet: benefits taxable up to 85%; given, not tested). Federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - 34,700.00 federal standard deduction (31,500 plus 2 x 1,600) = 65,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form M1, married filing jointly: line 1 federal AGI 100,000.00. Schedule M1M line 1 other-state municipal interest 0.00; line 10 additions 0.00; Form M1 line 2 0.00; line 3 = 100,000.00. Schedule M1M line 12: AGI 100,000.00 is not over 108,320.00, so worksheet steps 3-5 give 0 and the simplified amount is all of line 6b, 34,000.00. Alternative method, projection: measure = federal AGI + tax-exempt interest = 100,000.00 + 0.00 = 100,000.00; cap first: lesser of 34,000.00 and 5,840.00 = 5,840.00; less 20% x (excess over 88,630.00, 11,370.00) = 2,274.00; alternative = 3,566.00. Worksheet steps 9-24 as printed: steps 9-11 100,000.00 - 34,000.00 = 66,000.00; steps 12-13 50% x 40,000.00 = 20,000.00; step 14 0.00; step 15 86,000.00; steps 16-18 0.00; step 19 86,000.00; step 20 88,630.00; step 21 0.00; step 22 0.00; step 23 5,840.00; step 24 5,840.00; step 25-27 34,000.00; step 28 5,840.00; step 30 greater of 5,840.00 and 34,000.00 = 34,000.00. Line 12 = the better of the two, 34,000.00. The projection's alternative entry loses, so only the simplified amount is applied. Schedule M1R: line 1 12,000.00; line 2 0.00 (65 or older); line 3 12,000.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 nontaxable Social Security 40,000.00 - 34,000.00 = 6,000.00; line 6 Railroad Retirement Board benefits 0.00; line 7 6,000.00; line 8 = 6,000.00. Line 9 100,000.00; line 10 18,000.00; line 11 82,000.00; line 12 41,000.00; line 13 = 0.00. Schedule M1M line 40 = Form M1 line 7 subtractions = 34,000.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 = 34,000.00 (lines 12, 16, 17, 25). State income before deduction = 100,000.00 - 34,000.00 = 66,000.00. Standard Deduction Table for Line 4 (PDF p.13): base 29,900.00 plus 2 x 1,550 age box(es) = 33,000.00; AGI is not over 238,950.00, so no Worksheet A. Line 4 = 33,000.00. Form M1 line 8 total = 33,000.00 + 34,000.00 = 67,000.00; line 9 Minnesota taxable income = 100,000.00 - 67,000.00 = 33,000.00. Line 10 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.39): 5.35% x (33,000.00 - 0.00) = 1,765.50 = 1,765.50. The tax table (PDF pp.32-38) gives 1,768; expected keeps the schedule formula. Line 16 credits 0.00 (the joint-filer Schedule M1C credit is not in the sources and is not applied); state income tax 1,765.50.
accepted_approximations: Tax comes from the rate schedules at every income; below 86,800 of taxable income the booklet requires its 100-wide tax table.
The Schedule M1C credit for joint filers is not applied because its amount is not in the sources.
